Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Acute left-sided throbbing headache with preceding visual aura (zig-zag lines), photophobia, nausea, and two episodes of vomiting; worsened by movement/leaning forward. No fever, rash, trauma, or focal neurological symptoms reported. Prior similar episode a few weeks ago. Family history of migraine (mother). On combined oral contraceptive for 3 months.
- Most consistent with migraine with visual aura (high likelihood) based on phenotype and family history.
- Additional considerations from DDx (consistent with transcript):
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (moderate likelihood): New significant headache in a young woman on combined OCP; worse when leaning forward and associated with vomiting. Consider especially if headache persists, worsens, or neurological signs develop.
  - Subarachnoid hemorrhage (low likelihood): Acute severe headache with photophobia/vomiting; less likely given absence of thunderclap onset, prior similar episode, and no focal deficits.
- No examination findings or investigations documented today.
- Safety netting discussed: return if worsening over the next 2–3 days, not responding to medication, worsening neck pain, new weakness, or vision changes. Follow-up planned next week.
- Contraception: Discussion flagged by clinician; details not documented.

Management Plan
- Start symptomatic treatment: acetaminophen/paracetamol or co-codamol; NSAIDs such as ibuprofen or naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Keep a headache diary to identify triggers and track frequency/severity.
- Consider migraine prophylaxis if headaches become persistent or frequent; to be discussed at next visit.
- Follow-up: next week. Return earlier if symptoms worsen or red flags develop (as above).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Migraine with visual aura – High likelihood: Unilateral throbbing headache with classic visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, worsened by activity; prior similar episode; family history.
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) – Moderate likelihood: New significant headache in young woman on combined OCP; worse on leaning forward with vomiting; consider if atypical course or neurological signs emerge.
- Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) – Low likelihood: Acute severe headache with photophobia/vomiting, but no thunderclap onset, no focal deficits, and prior similar episode.
